scope: A purposive context register; not a sampled comparison corpus or an ancestry ranking.

sources.title: Dances with Cranes: animal masquerade in Pre-Pottery Neolithic ritual
sources.author: Jens Notroff / German Archaeological Institute
sources.note: Excavation-team discussion of Pillars 2, 33, 38 and 56. Masking, dance and transformation are interpretations; the carved birds are observations. Indexed full text checked; direct host did not resolve in this session.

sources.title: Of animals and a headless man: Pillar 43
sources.author: Oliver Dietrich / Göbekli Tepe Research Project
sources.note: Motifs and competing readings of the disc. The author’s 17 October 2016 reply discusses possible later regional continuities while stressing missing links.

sources.title: Painted slabs from the ceremonial village of Orongo
sources.author: Museo Antropológico Padre Sebastián Englert, Rapa Nui
sources.note: Identifies MAPSE 17-00-1312 as two facing tangata manu from a house at Orongo, brought to the museum in 1974 during restoration. That is a collection event, not the painting date.

sources.title: Rapa Nui MAPSE 17-00-1312 · 3D recording
sources.author: Factum Foundation; linked by the Rapa Nui museum
sources.note: Model identity, creator and preview verified through the public Sketchfab API. The preview is a textured 3D rendering, not an excavation photograph or an AI reconstruction. No open reuse licence is stated.

sources.title: The Mystery of Easter Island · figures 110 and 112; pages 261–263
sources.author: Katherine Routledge / Mana Expedition
sources.note: Historical photographs and interpreted birdman traditions, recorded through Rapanui interlocutors. Figure 110 reproduces the same carved surface as the existing Mata Ngarau image; these are not independent examples.

sources.title: Hoa Hakananai’a · Oc1869,1005.1
sources.author: British Museum
sources.note: Identity and carved motifs; distinguish the statue from subsequent carving episodes. Exact motif dates are unresolved.

sources.title: Birdman boulder · Oc1920,0506.1
sources.author: British Museum / Google Arts & Culture
sources.note: Orongo provenance and egg interpretation. The catalogue range 1750–1875 is approximate, not a direct measurement of carving age.

sources.title: Update on the Hoa Hakananai’a statue
sources.author: James Miles / Archaeological Computing Research Group, Southampton
sources.note: Research team’s photogrammetry and reflectance-transformation imaging. The original top-back RTI link returned HTTP 403 on this check; its existence does not mean the dataset was successfully examined here.

sources.title: From Monuments to Miniatures: Emergence of Stamps and Related Image-bearing Objects during the Neolithic
sources.author: Çiğdem Atakuman
sources.note: Author’s university record and abstract checked, DOI 10.1017/S0959774315000396. A regional continuity lead; its full object sequence has not been audited for this project.

objects.name: Pillar 43
objects.date_scope: Early Neolithic context; site broadly tenth–ninth millennium BCE. Context is not a direct carving date.
objects.observation: Prominent bird, disc above an extended wing, another nearby bird; scorpion and three arched forms elsewhere on the surface.
objects.relevance: The focal bird-and-disc composition. Its disc has several published interpretations.

objects.name: Pillar 2
objects.date_scope: Early Neolithic site context; no motif-specific date established here.
objects.observation: A crane below a fox and aurochs. The excavation team discusses its unusual legs.
objects.relevance: Birds with humanlike traits have a local comparison beyond Pillar 43.

objects.name: Pillar 33
objects.date_scope: Early Neolithic site context; no motif-specific date established here.
objects.observation: The source illustrates a crane with thick, bent legs.
objects.relevance: A second local anatomical variant. Species and performance interpretations need checking against the carving.
objects.inspection: Source description; new photograph not acquired

objects.name: Pillar 38
objects.date_scope: Early Neolithic site context; no motif-specific date established here.
objects.observation: The source describes three birds, at least two with unusual legs.
objects.relevance: Repeated birds within the same site; not three independent artefacts.
objects.inspection: Source description; new photograph not acquired

objects.name: Pillar 56
objects.date_scope: Early Neolithic site context; no motif-specific date established here.
objects.observation: The source contrasts these birds’ more naturalistic legs with those on other pillars.
objects.relevance: A local contrast, useful for testing a broad claim that all the birds are humans in costume.
objects.inspection: Source description; new photograph not acquired

objects.name: Hoa Hakananai’a · back
objects.context: Orongo · formerly in the house Taura Renga
objects.date_scope: Birdman carvings are later than the original statue. Removed from Rapa Nui in 1868; exact carving dates uncertain.
objects.observation: Two principal birdman figures, a smaller central bird and a large ring below the main figures.
objects.relevance: An arrangement of figures and symbols; the ring is not visibly held like the boulder’s rounded object.

objects.name: Birdman boulder
objects.date_scope: Carved by its 1914 excavation; catalogue range 1750–1875 is approximate.
objects.observation: A bird-headed figure with a rounded object at the hand, interpreted as an egg.
objects.relevance: The more specific comparison with Pillar 43: a birdlike figure next to a rounded object and an extended limb.

objects.name: Mata Ngarau rock
objects.date_scope: Present when photographed during the 1914–15 expedition. Carving date not established here.
objects.observation: Three bird-headed figures occur together on the photographed surface.
objects.relevance: Local repetition of the figure type. The two reproductions count as one surface.
objects.inspection: Two reproductions of the same historic photograph

objects.name: Painted Orongo slab
objects.context: Orongo house; now Museo Rapa Nui
objects.date_scope: Moved to the museum in 1974. The consulted record does not specify the painting date.
objects.observation: Two facing tangata manu, identified by the Rapa Nui museum.
objects.relevance: The paired birdman arrangement appears on another local object and in a different medium.
objects.inspection: Museum record and preview of Factum Foundation’s 3D recording
